# Where this comes from

## We built the modular one already

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
- I started `epinowcast` in 2021 to be the modular one. The repository
  description still says "a modular Bayesian framework for real-time
  infectious disease surveillance"
- It was modular in the sense I meant then. Every component had a
  regression interface and could be switched out
- It still cannot be taken apart into pieces anyone else can use
- Large API, hard to contribute to, hard to adapt past what it already
  supports, and limited in scope despite the ambition

::: {.callout-important}
The unit of reuse was the whole model, not the epidemiological ideas
inside it.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
- Before that, `EpiNow2`. After it, `primarycensored` and `epidist`
- Each one found a real problem, fixed it, and left behind another
  package that could not be pulled apart
- Five years of that. The fix is always a new package

::: {.attribution}
[epinowcast/epinowcast](https://github.com/epinowcast/epinowcast),
created 2021-10-29 ·
[epiforecasts/EpiNow2](https://github.com/epiforecasts/EpiNow2),
created 2020-06-17
:::
:::
::::

## The same request, five and a half years apart

- **EpiNow2 #122**, October 2020, opened by me. Split the Stan code into
  functions "as adding extensions/reusing code will be easier"
- **EpiNow2 #1345**, April 2026, opened by me. `epinow()` "orchestrates
  sequential calls rather than fitting a joint model". Still open
- The joint model has been written down as an issue three times in four
  years. None of them landed, because doing it means rewriting the
  package
- **#1268** asks us to vendor `primarycensored`'s Stan code into
  EpiNow2. Sharing a component between two Stan packages means copying
  its source in

::: {.callout-note}
Almost all of these are opened by maintainers, not users. Users ask for
features. We convert those into structural work that never ships.
:::

## It is not only us

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- Several packages estimate the reproduction number with renewal
  approaches in Stan. None share components. Some share authors
- Wastewater tools are mostly written by people who are not wastewater
  experts. An expert who wants to contribute has to write a whole model
- Delay estimation, nowcasting, viral load, severity, forecasting. Each
  rebuilds the same parts under different names
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
- We wrote down a workflow for building these models, then found we
  could not follow it with the tools we had built
- The paper says so itself. We provided a schematic case study, not
  code, because the software to do it did not exist

::: {.callout-important}
The ecosystem is the attempt to make our own workflow followable.
:::
